$comment: Seconds each browser test file runs in one of CI's docs browser jobs (4 cores, the files several at a time, so the time a file takes beside others): what packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js splits the files into TEST_SHARD's shares by (`--shard-weights`, apps/docs/package.json's test:browser), longest first, each to the share with the least so far. A file not named here weighs the median of these, and the log of its job says so. A name of a file that is not here is ignored. Every file but the five of lists and menus (below) measured again from CI on 2026-11-28, from the `# file-duration` lines of the ten docs browser jobs of run 46123921832 (all green; packages/tools/src/shard-weights.js). Before that, every file was measured from CI on 2026-11-27, from the `# file-duration` lines of the green docs browser jobs of three train runs: 45955214109 and 45985598770 (all ten jobs green) and 45993351303 (nine green; its eighth job reached its time limit and printed none), the mean of the runs that ran the file (held-room-calendar: the last only, before its file reached main). In those runs a job's test time was close to what its files take run in name order, three at a time (within 5 s for each of the 14 green shared jobs); a job now starts its files longest first by these weights (run-node-tests.js, longestFirst), which by those runs' seconds brings each shared job within 2 % of the best three at a time can do (packages/tools/test/fixtures/docs-browser-jobs.json). The eighth job of 45993351303 was planned at 1627 s by the weights before these, several of them measured on a Mac; by these its files weigh 2145 s, three at a time about 940 s, and in that run they ran 15 to 45 % slower still. The same file's seconds differ by up to a third between runs (focus-order 559 to 787, tokens-table 147 to 353), and files measured on an 11-core Mac took 1.1 to 1.4 times as long in CI (held-room-buttons 450 → 539, held-room-actions 422 → 591) and up to 2.6 times for files that load many pages (blueprint 109 → 286, blueprint-pages 93 → 240): a weight measured locally is a floor, not the file's CI seconds, and is measured again from CI once a run's jobs are green. Six were weighed so until run 46123921832 measured them. blueprint-pages reads every measure figure in each preset as well since 2026-11-27: it weighed its CI seconds above scaled by its local runs alone before and after that (86 s and 165 s), 240 × 165 / 86. held-room-measures and held-room-anatomy were new, and weighed their local seconds times 1.25 for CI, about what the held-room files measured on the Mac took there (held-room-figures 375 → 412, held-room-buttons 450 → 539, held-room-actions 422 → 591): held-room-measures 191 s in a local run alone, beside held-room-tables' 820 s, scaled by that file's Mac weight then (812 × 191 / 820 = 189; 189 × 1.25 = 236), held-room-anatomy 95 s in a local run of it alone (`--test-concurrency=2`, its pages in the three engines; 95 × 1.25 = 119), and held-room-chips 429 s alone, its three engines one after another, as a job runs a file, on a Mac that other runs kept at a load of 11 to 16 (429 × 1.25 = 536); held-room-fields and held-room-file-items-tabs were one file in CI run 46092662572 (which took 1057 s of its eighth job's 20 minutes, its three engines one after another, and left its other files too little: the job reached its limit), and were first weighed by the sum of their pages' tests in that job's log, before run 46123921832 measured them. held-room-list, held-room-list-cupertino, held-room-menu, held-room-menu-cupertino and held-room-menubar were one file too (held-room-lists, the pages of lists, menus and menu bars), which ran 19 minutes of its job's 20 in CI run 46127525694 on 2026-11-28, its three engines one after another, and reached the job's limit in WebKit with one test left. Each weighs the sum of its pages' tests in that job's log (its sixth), each engine's, and each engine's launch in that log (its describe's seconds less its tests': Chromium 7.9 s, Firefox 0.8 s; WebKit, whose describe that job did not finish, 0.8 s in run 46123921832's ninth job, which ran the whole file); the Menubar's page at a phone's width in WebKit, which that job did not reach, weighs its 29.2 s in run 46123921832 times 1.27, what WebKit's six other tests of the file took in the one run over the other (460.7 s over 361.4 s): held-room-list 246 s (Chromium 55.2, Firefox 68.2, WebKit 113.0, and the launches), held-room-list-cupertino 144 s, held-room-menu 249 s, held-room-menu-cupertino 305 s and held-room-menubar 217 s. The Menu's page in cupertino is one page at one width, and the heaviest file: its WebKit test alone took 126.5 s. Keep them current: a file they do not weigh, or weigh at half its time, lands in a job it overfills. To measure them again: every job sharded by these weights prints `# file-duration <file> <seconds>` (the duration of the file's own run) at the end of its log; save the logs of a run's jobs (`gh run view -R <owner>/<repo> --job <job> --log > shard-N.log`, or `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/jobs/<job>/logs > shard-N.log`: either can come back empty or end in a stream error, so count each log's `# file-duration` lines) and run `node packages/tools/src/shard-weights.js apps/docs/test/browser/durations.json shard-1.log shard-2.log shard-3.log`. `$alone` lists the files that take a CI job of their own (packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js, balance): the fixture gallery keeps the job's cores busy for its whole run, and beside it the Button page took more than 30 s to load in WebKit (run 40329390452), so it runs alone and the others share the remaining jobs. The two previews files run alone for the same reason: each draws four pages at a time in Chromium, rastered on the CPU, for its whole run, and beside either one the Button page took 20 to 35 s to load in WebKit and Firefox, often more than `goto`'s 30 s (the Do and Don't, appearance and one-frame tests, in CI and in the CI image). The icon font's test runs alone for the same reason: it opens every built page, four at a time in Chromium, for its whole run, and beside it the Button page took 20 to 32 s to load in WebKit in CI (its share of runs 42696507478, 42708250670 and 42741065358, the last over `goto`'s 30 s); in the CI image on 2 CPUs, its share's files, run as CI runs them, failed 5 to 10 tests in each of 5 runs, the Button page taking 24 to 36 s in WebKit; without it, its other files (once) and the shares the page foot's test has had since (four runs) failed none but the sitemap's test, which dates pages by a commit history the image's copy does not have, the Button page taking 8 to 16 s. The reader's own theme runs alone for the other side of it: it measures how soon a press is drawn (150 ms), and beside other files WebKit drew it in 170 to 210 ms (CI run 42752233102; the CI image on 2 CPUs, three runs of four, two files at a time as well as three), where alone it drew it in 36 to 55 ms (the CI image, five runs measured, and none of eight runs alone failed).
